text: Jim stood in the back of the advanced yoga studio, sweating profusely as he attempted to mimic the instructor’s perfect downward dog. The room was silent, save for the soft hum of meditation, until Jim’s stomach gave a loud, resonant gurgle. He tried to ignore it, shifting his weight, but the pressure built. With a focused grunt, he attempted to hold a complex balance pose, only to release a sound so distinct and prolonged that the instructor paused mid-stretch. The class erupted in suppressed giggles, breaking the zen atmosphere. Jim, mortified, looked around for an escape, but his eyes landed on the only creature in the room that seemed unfazed by the chaos: a large, long-necked giraffe statue in the corner, which stared back with an expression of serene judgment, as if to say, "At least I don't have to hold my breath."
